title: Saying what happened without naming the doer

sections.title: Three tools
sections.content: You know how to say what happened without naming the doer from B2 Unit 15: *bocsátottak el* is the third person plural with no subject. News and workplace texts use one of three constructions, and this lesson adds the vocabulary of layoffs and the habit of simplifying officialese. The active verb in the third person plural with no subject: *háromszáz dolgozót bocsátottak el* ('three hundred workers were laid off'), where 'they' means nobody in particular. A *-va/-ve* form with *van* for a resulting state: *a gyár kapui le vannak zárva* ('the factory gates are locked'). And, in official reports, *kerül* with a verbal noun in *-ra/-re*: *a túlórák kifizetésre kerültek* ('the overtime was paid'). That last one is correct but heavy.

sections.title: In labour news
rows: Three hundred workers were laid off.
Wages were frozen for a year.
A gyár kapui le vannak zárva.
A kollektív szerződés alá van írva.

sections.content: In the third-person-plural construction the thing affected stays the object, in the accusative: *a béreket befagyasztották*, not *a bérek befagyasztották*. Don't build an English-style passive with *lett* (*a sztrájk be lett tiltva*) in written Hungarian either: say *betiltották a sztrájkot*. If you do want to name the doer, make it the subject: *a vezetőség befagyasztotta a béreket*. For the *kerül* construction, most editors prefer the plain verb: *kifizették a túlórákat*.
